No code is authored into the tree (every concrete module is a later step's job), `src/placeholder.ts` is preserved, and the existing lint/typecheck/test commands behave exactly as they do today (this step neither fixes nor worsens their known baseline failures).

- Add a zero-byte `.gitkeep` file to each of the nine new empty directories so the §3 layout survives commit/clone (git cannot track empty dirs; `.gitkeep` files are transient scaffolding, have no lint/type/test impact, and are not excluded by `.gitignore`) [from: Q2]

```sh
set -eu
fail() { echo "FAIL: $1"; exit 1; }
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

# Capture a pre-change snapshot of the protected files so byte-for-byte equality can be asserted
# even when they are not yet committed (git show HEAD: only works on committed blobs).
snap_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$snap_dir"' EXIT
for f in package.json tsconfig.json eslint.config.js .prettierrc.cjs src/placeholder.ts; do
  cp "$f" "$snap_dir/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')"
done

# 1) All nine new directories exist
for d in src/shared src/server src/server/routes src/server/migrations src/client src/client/components src/client/components/ui src/client/pages test; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || fail "missing directory: $d"
done

# 2) Exactly one zero-byte .gitkeep in each new directory, and each holds nothing else
for d in src/shared src/server src/server/routes src/server/migrations src/client src/client/components src/client/components/ui src/client/pages test; do
  f="$d/.gitkeep"
  [ -f "$f" ] || fail "missing .gitkeep in $d"
  [ "$(wc -c < "$f")" -eq 0 ] || fail ".gitkeep in $d is not zero-byte"
  [ "$(find "$d" -mindepth 1 -type f | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] || fail "$d contains files other than .gitkeep"
done
# No .gitkeep anywhere else in the repo (outside node_modules): exactly nine total, one per new dir
[ "$(find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -name .gitkeep -print | wc -l)" -eq 9 ] \
  || fail "expected exactly 9 .gitkeep files, got $(find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -name .gitkeep -print | wc -l)"

# 3) No concrete §3 file was pre-scaffolded
for f in src/shared/schema.ts src/server/index.ts src/server/db.ts src/server/migrate.ts src/server/seed.ts src/server/auth.ts src/server/images.ts src/server/routes/auth.ts src/server/routes/invites.ts src/server/routes/listings.ts src/server/routes/photos.ts src/server/routes/admin.ts src/client/main.tsx src/client/api.ts src/client/index.css; do
  [ -e "$f" ] && fail "pre-created later-step file: $f"
done
[ -z "$(find src/server/migrations -name '*.sql' -print)" ] || fail "pre-created migration .sql file"

# 4) placeholder.ts preserved and no test files added
[ -f src/placeholder.ts ] || fail "src/placeholder.ts missing"
[ -z "$(find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o \( -name '*.test.ts' -o -name '*.spec.ts' \) -print)" ] || fail "test file added"

# 5) No second package.json under src/ or test/
[ -z "$(find src test -name package.json -print)" ] || fail "stray package.json under src/ or test/"

# 6) Protected root configs + placeholder byte-identical to their pre-change content.
#    Prefer the committed blob when present (catches even uncommitted edits); otherwise the
#    snapshot taken at the top of this script (catches edits whether or not the file is committed).
#    No branch may fall through to a no-op: every file must match, and a missing committed blob
#    must fall back to the snapshot — never skip the assertion.
for f in package.json tsconfig.json eslint.config.js .prettierrc.cjs src/placeholder.ts; do
  sum_a=$(sha256sum "$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)
  sum_b=$(git show "HEAD:$f" 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
  if [ -z "$sum_b" ]; then
    sum_b=$(sha256sum "$snap_dir/$(echo "$f" | tr '/' '_')" | cut -d' ' -f1)
    [ -n "$sum_b" ] || fail "no pre-change reference available for $f"
  fi
  [ "$sum_a" = "$sum_b" ] || fail "$f changed from its pre-change baseline (current=$sum_a baseline=$sum_b)"
done

# 7) Baseline tooling behavior is UNCHANGED: empty dirs contribute zero input files, so both
#    must still fail exactly as before (prettier zero-glob / tsc TS18003), neither fixed nor newly broken.
bun run lint >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "bun run lint unexpectedly succeeded (baseline should still fail: prettier zero-glob / tsc TS18003)"
tsc_out=$(bunx tsc --noEmit 2>&1) || true
echo "$tsc_out" | grep -q "TS18003" || fail "tsc did not fail with TS18003 'No inputs were found' as in the pre-change baseline (got: $tsc_out)"

echo "ALL DIR-TREE CHECKS PASSED"
```

spec:
GOAL

Create the local-dev infrastructure slice for the MX-5 Private marketplace at the repo root: a `docker-compose.dev.yml` that brings up a single Postgres 18 container exposing BOTH the dev database and a separate `mx5_test` database (created by a no-migration init mechanism — e.g. init SQL mounted into `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/` — because `migrate.ts` is a later step and must not be assumed), and a `.env` file supplying exactly the five design-named runtime variables (`DATABASE_URL`, `APP_URL`, `PORT`, `ADMIN_PHONE`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`) with values self-consistent with the compose file (the exact host, port, credentials, and dev-database name that `DATABASE_URL` points at). The `dev` script in `package.json` already exists and matches design §9 verbatim — verify it and leave it untouched. Done looks like: `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d` starts a reachable Postgres 18 instance on which BOTH the dev database and `mx5_test` exist, and `.env` provides every variable the later `db.ts`/`migrate.ts`/`seed.ts`/invite-URL steps will read, with `DATABASE_URL` pointing at the exact host:port the compose file publishes.

CONSTRAINTS

- `docker-compose.dev.yml` at the repo root must run a single `postgres` service using the image `postgres:18` (the design pins "Postgres 18 (latest stable, 18.4 as of 2026-07)" and does not force a sub-version; do not invent one). [from: spec]
- The compose file must create BOTH the dev database AND a separate `mx5_test` database (design §10: tests run against a "separate `mx5_test` database (same docker-compose Postgres)") using a no-migration mechanism (init SQL mounted into `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/` and/or `POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS`), not a migration file. [from: spec]
- `.env` must contain exactly the five named variables `DATABASE_URL`, `APP_URL`, `PORT`, `ADMIN_PHONE`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD` — no extra invented variables. [from: spec]
- `DATABASE_URL` must be a plain `postgresql://user:pass@<host>:<port>/<db>` URL (Bun's built-in SQL client; there is no `bun:sql` module) whose host, port, and credentials match exactly what `docker-compose.dev.yml` publishes, and it must point at the dev database (not `mx5_test`). [from: spec]
- The `POSTGRES_USER`/`POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in the compose file must match the user/password encoded in `DATABASE_URL`, and that user must be the image superuser so the later `pg_trgm` GIN-index migration (design §4) can `CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm`. [from: spec]
- The app `PORT` in `.env` must NOT equal the Postgres published host port in the compose file (distinct ports). [from: spec]
- `APP_URL` in `.env` must be `http://localhost:<PORT>` using the app port value from the same file, with no trailing path or slash, so invite links built in a later step as `APP_URL + /join/:token` resolve locally. [from: spec]
- `ADMIN_PHONE` must be valid E.164 matching `/^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$/` (e.g. `+37120000000`), since a later seed step hashes `ADMIN_PHONE`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD` directly into the root admin account. [from: spec]
- `.env` is the local-secret file to create; it is already gitignored (`.gitignore` has `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example`) — do NOT add a `.env.example` (the design names none) and do not commit real secrets beyond reasonable local defaults. [from: spec]
- `package.json` is authoritative and already complete: do not add, remove, rename, or re-scope any existing script or dependency. The `dev` script already encodes the required "concurrent watch: tailwind, bun build, server" behavior; keep it exactly as-is. [from: spec]
- Keep the compose file minimal: a single `postgres` service, a named or bind-mounted data volume, an init mechanism for `mx5_test`; no extra services (no pgAdmin, no adminer, no extra containers); a healthcheck is acceptable but not required. [from: spec]
- Do NOT edit anything under `src/`, `test/`, or `ct/`, or touch `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `.prettierrc.cjs`, `playwright-ct.config.ts`. [from: spec]
- Do NOT create `.env.example`. [from: spec]

ACCEPTANCE

- `docker-compose.dev.yml` exists at the repo root and is a valid Compose file that defines exactly one service (the Postgres one). [static]
- The `postgres` service uses image `postgres:18` and publishes a host port. [static]
- `.env` exists at the repo root and contains exactly the five keys `DATABASE_URL`, `APP_URL`, `PORT`, `ADMIN_PHONE`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`. [static]
- `DATABASE_URL` in `.env` points at `localhost` on the exact host port the compose file publishes, with the same credentials and the dev database name (not `mx5_test`). [static]
- `PORT` in `.env` does not equal the Postgres published host port in the compose file. [static]
- `ADMIN_PHONE` in `.env` satisfies `/^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$/`. [static]
- `APP_URL` in `.env` equals `http://localhost:<PORT>` where `<PORT>` is the app port value in the same file (no trailing path). [static]
- After `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d`, the container answers `pg_isready` on its published host port and reports a PostgreSQL 18 server. [cmd: docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T postgres pg_isready && docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -tAc "SELECT version()"]
- After a fresh `up -d`, BOTH the dev database and `mx5_test` exist on the running instance (created by the init mechanism, not a migration file). [cmd: docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -tAc "SELECT datname FROM pg_database"]
- `.env.example` was not created by this slice. [static]
- `package.json` `dev` script is unchanged and still matches design §9 verbatim (no script added/removed/renamed). [static]
- The existing repo lint gate still passes after this change (no `src/`/`test/`/config edits were made). [cmd: bun run lint]

VERIFY:
```sh
set -eu

# 1. Compose file is valid YAML/config and pins postgres:18
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml config --quiet
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml config --images | grep -qx 'postgres:18'

# 2. Bring up the dev Postgres (fresh volume so init SQL runs)
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml ps

# 3. Wait for readiness inside the container, confirm PostgreSQL 18
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T postgres pg_isready -q && break
  sleep 2
done
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T postgres pg_isready
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T postgres psql -U "${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT version()" | grep -q "PostgreSQL 18"

# 4. BOTH the dev database and mx5_test exist (init mechanism, not a migration file)
DBS="$(docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T postgres psql -U "${POSTGRES_USER:-postgres}" -tAc "SELECT datname FROM pg_database")"
echo "$DBS" | grep -qx mx5_test

# 5. .env supplies exactly the five required vars and is self-consistent with compose
for k in DATABASE_URL APP_URL PORT ADMIN_PHONE ADMIN_PASSWORD; do grep -q "^${k}=" .env; done
[ "$(grep -Ec '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' .env)" -eq 5 ]
grep -Eq '^PORT=[0-9]+$' .env
grep -Eq '^ADMIN_PHONE=\+[1-9][0-9]{6,14}$' .env

# Parse the compose-published host port and DB user from the rendered config
HOST_PORT="$(docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml config --format json | sed -n 's/.*"published"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}\([0-9]\{1,5\}\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
DB_USER="$(docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml config --format json | sed -n 's/.*"POSTGRES_USER"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}\([^"]\{1,64\}\).*/\1/p' | head -n1)"

# DATABASE_URL points at the compose-published host port on localhost with the compose DB user
grep -Eq "^DATABASE_URL=postgresql://${DB_USER}:[^@]+@localhost:${HOST_PORT}/[^/]+$" .env

# APP_URL is http://localhost:<PORT> with no trailing path
grep -Eq "^APP_URL=http://localhost:$(grep '^PORT=' .env | cut -d= -f2)$" .env

# App PORT does not collide with the Postgres host port
[ "$(grep '^PORT=' .env | cut -d= -f2)" != "${HOST_PORT}" ]

# 6. No extra services: the rendered config has exactly one top-level service block
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml config --format json | grep -q '"services"'
[ "$(docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml config --format json | grep -Ec '^\s{4}"[a-z0-9_-]+":\s*\{')" -eq 1 ]

# 7. package.json dev script unchanged (verbatim match to design section 9)
grep -Fq '"dev": "bunx @tailwindcss/cli -i src/client/index.css -o dist/app.css --watch & bun run --watch build.ts & bun run --watch src/server/index.ts & wait"' package.json

# 8. This slice did not create the sibling artifacts later steps own (they are absent at this point in the plan)
[ ! -e .env.example ]

# 9. Existing repo lint gate still passes (no src/test/config edits made)
bun run lint
```

spec:
GOAL
Create `src/server/db.ts` — the project's single database access layer — using Bun's built-in Postgres client, connected from the `DATABASE_URL` env var (already in `.env`, read at module load), and add `test/db.test.ts` in the same change. The module exports the shared `sql` handle plus four minimal typed, parameterized helpers — `queryAll<T>`, `queryFirst<T>` (returns `T | undefined`), `queryOne<T>` (rejects unless exactly one row), and a thin `withTransaction<T>` over `sql.begin` — all built on the `sql<T[]>(...)` tagged template so later steps (migrate step 8, seed step 10, routes 15–32) import their DB connection and query primitives from this one file. Done looks like: `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes with both new files in the tree, both are formatted per `.prettierrc.cjs` (4-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, printWidth 120) and pass ESLint (`no-explicit-any: error`, `no-shadow: error`), and `bun run test` exits 0 — the new test proves reachability of the dev `mx5` Postgres 18 and that each helper executes a parameterized query, and the existing `playwright-ct.config.ts`-driven `test:ct` half keeps passing.

CONSTRAINTS
- The module MUST be `src/server/db.ts`, exactly as pinned in the design's repo layout; create no other source file except the same-change test `test/db.test.ts`. No routes, schemas, migration files, tables, or components. [from: spec]
- Connect via Bun's built-in SQL client: `import { sql } from "bun"` (and `import type { SQL } from "bun"` if a type annotation is needed — required under `verbatimModuleSyntax`). There is NO `bun:sql` module. [from: spec]
- Read the connection string from `DATABASE_URL` (`postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/mx5`, already in `.env`, auto-loaded by Bun). Eager connection at module load is acceptable since `.env` is required. Do not add a new env var; do not change `.env`, `docker-compose.dev.yml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `.prettierrc.cjs`, or `playwright-ct.config.ts`. [from: spec]
- Every query MUST go through the Bun SQL tagged template (`sql\`... ${param} ...``). String interpolation/concatenation of user values into SQL is forbidden. [from: spec]
- Do NOT create or depend on: `src/server/migrate.ts`, `src/server/seed.ts`, `src/server/auth.ts`, `src/shared/schema.ts`, anything under `src/server/routes/`, any SQL migration file, or any table — those are later steps. `db.ts` must compile and connect with zero tables existing (the dev `mx5` database is empty until step 9). [from: spec]
- Keep the module server-side only (`src/server/**` ESLint glob with `globals.node`); do not import anything from `src/client` or `src/shared` (`schema.ts` does not exist yet). [from: spec]
- The helper test lands in the same change and passes; the task is not done until `bun run test` exits 0. [from: spec]
- The test connects through the exported shared `sql` handle and runs `SELECT 1` plus a parameterized round-trip directly against the dev `mx5` database from `DATABASE_URL` — `mx5_test` only exists via the later step-13 test harness, and the constraints forbid new tables/migrations; the test must have no dependency on any later-step infrastructure. [from: Q3]
- Helper surface is option B: export the shared `sql` handle plus minimal typed parameterized helpers — `queryAll<T>` (awaits `sql<T[]>`), `queryFirst<T>` (returns `Promise<T | undefined>`, not a non-null assert), `queryOne<T>` (rejects unless exactly one row), and a thin `withTransaction<T>` wrapper over `sql.begin`. Re-export the `SQL` type only if needed; helpers are additive so later steps can call `sql` directly if a helper does not fit. [from: Q1]
- `withTransaction<T>` exists because seed (step 10) and multi-statement route flows will need transactions; keep every helper explicit-generic so no implicit `any` leaks into the exported surface. [from: Q2]
- Helpers MUST be built on `await sql<T[]>(...)` — awaiting a `SQL.Query<T>` resolves directly to `T[]`; there is no `SQLQueryResult` wrapper, no `.rows` property, and `.get()`, `.all()`, `.run()` are NOT declared in the installed `bun-types` 1.4.2 — do not call or reference them. [from: Q1]
- Use `import { sql } from "bun"`; `bun:sql` is not a module — do not import it or declare a module for it. [from: Q1]
- The tagged-template generic `T` is explicit and never inferred from the template string (`<T = any>(strings, ...values): SQL.Query<T>`), so every helper must pass an explicit generic to keep the surface `any`-free under `no-explicit-any: error`. [from: Q2]
- `queryFirst<T>` must type its return as `Promise<T | undefined>` — with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` active, destructuring the first element of the awaited `T[]` yields `T | undefined`, so no non-null assertion is allowed. [from: Q1]
- Formatting follows `.prettierrc.cjs` exactly: 4 spaces (`tabWidth 4`, no tabs), no semicolons, single quotes, `printWidth 120`, no bracket spacing, `arrowParens: avoid`, LF. [from: spec]
- ESLint typed rules are errors on this file: `no-explicit-any: error`, `@typescript-eslint/no-shadow: error`; `tsc --noEmit` runs under `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`. [from: spec]
- `db.ts` does no Zod validation of route-level input (downstream callers validate their own inputs per §11), but must be typed so untyped/`any` parameters are rejected — no `any` in this file. [from: spec]
- `updated_at` is set by the app on every UPDATE (no trigger), so no trigger-based or table-specific helpers may be built for tables owned by later steps; helpers stay table-agnostic. [from: spec]

ACCEPTANCE
- `src/server/db.ts` exists and exports the shared `sql` handle (type `SQL` from `"bun"`) plus the four helpers `queryAll`, `queryFirst`, `queryOne`, `withTransaction`. [static]
- `test/db.test.ts` exists, imports the module under test, and contains one test titled for each of the five behaviours below plus the connectivity check. [test: test/db.test.ts "connects to the dev database through the shared sql handle"]
- `queryAll<T>(...)` awaits `sql<T[]>(...)` and resolves directly to the row array with no `.rows` wrapper; the test passes a bound parameter (e.g. `SELECT ${n} AS n`) and asserts the returned array carries the value back. [test: test/db.test.ts "queryAll returns rows from a parameterized query"]
- `queryFirst<T>(...)` resolves to `T | undefined`: the first row when the query matches one, `undefined` when it matches none (no non-null assert, safe under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`). [test: test/db.test.ts "queryFirst returns undefined when no row matches"]
- `queryOne<T>(...)` resolves to the single row when exactly one matches and rejects when the result is not exactly one row. [test: test/db.test.ts "queryOne rejects when zero rows match"]
- `withTransaction<T>(fn)` runs the callback with a scoped `TransactionSQL` and resolves with the callback's return value (thin wrapper over `sql.begin`); the test issues a parameterized query inside the callback and asserts the resolved value equals the callback's return. [test: test/db.test.ts "withTransaction runs a parameterized query and resolves with the callback return value"]
- The shared `sql` handle is reachable against the live dev Postgres: importing the module and awaiting a `SELECT 1`-style query through the exported `sql` succeeds. [test: test/db.test.ts "connects to the dev database through the shared sql handle"]
- `bun run test` exits 0 — the new `test/db.test.ts` passes under `bun test` AND the existing `playwright test -c playwright-ct.config.ts` half (including the dual-runned `ct/smoke.spec.tsx` bun test) stays green. [cmd: bun run test]
- Strict typecheck passes with `src/server/db.ts` and `test/db.test.ts` in the tree. [cmd: bunx tsc --noEmit]
- `bun run lint` exits 0: Prettier formats cleanly, ESLint reports no `no-explicit-any` / `no-shadow` errors on the new files, and `tsc --noEmit` passes. [cmd: bun run lint]
- Both new files are Prettier-clean per `.prettierrc.cjs` (4-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, printWidth 120). [cmd: bunx prettier --check src/server/db.ts test/db.test.ts]

VERIFY:
```sh
set -e
# Postgres 18 must be up and healthy before any gate (dev db mx5 is created by the compose service).
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --wait

# --- Structure: both files exist and the module uses the built-in client, not bun:sql ---
test -f src/server/db.ts
test -f test/db.test.ts
grep -q 'from "bun"' src/server/db.ts
! grep -q 'bun:sql' src/server/db.ts

# --- The test actually exercises the four helpers (not just a connectivity ping) ---
grep -q 'queryAll' test/db.test.ts
grep -q 'queryFirst' test/db.test.ts
grep -q 'queryOne' test/db.test.ts
grep -q 'withTransaction' test/db.test.ts
grep -Eq 'SELECT \\\$\{|\\\$\{.*\}.*SELECT|SELECT[^a-zA-Z]*\\\$\{' test/db.test.ts  # a bound parameter is used in at least one query

# --- Gate 1: strict typecheck (EXPECT: exit 0; any failure = FAIL) ---
bunx tsc --noEmit || { echo "FAIL: tsc --noEmit"; exit 1; }

# --- Gate 2: lint (prettier --write + eslint --fix + tsc; EXPECT: exit 0) ---
bun run lint || { echo "FAIL: bun run lint"; exit 1; }

# --- Gate 3: prettier formatting is clean (the half the lint script rewrites, so check idempotency) ---
bunx prettier --check src/server/db.ts test/db.test.ts || { echo "FAIL: prettier --check"; exit 1; }

# --- Gate 4: full test suite (bun test half incl. db.test.ts + playwright-ct half; EXPECT: exit 0) ---
bun run test || { echo "FAIL: bun run test"; exit 1; }
echo "PASS: all gates green"
```

spec:
GOAL
Create `src/server/migrate.ts`, the SQL migrations runner for the MX-5 Private project, executed by the already-existing `migrate` script in `package.json` (`bun run src/server/migrate.ts`). It exports `runMigrations(migrationsDir?: string)` (default `import.meta.dir + '/migrations'`), guarded by a direct-execution check (`if (import.meta.main)`) so `bun run migrate` auto-runs it with the default. When run it connects to the Postgres database named by the existing `DATABASE_URL` env var through the existing `sql` client exported from `./db.ts` (never a second `import { sql } from 'bun'`), ensures the `schema_migrations` tracking table exists (design §4: "Migrations are tracked in a `schema_migrations` table by `migrate.ts`"), then discovers and applies every unapplied `.sql` file in the given directory in ascending lexicographic filename order. Each file is applied in its own transaction (via the existing `withTransaction` helper) with its filename recorded in `schema_migrations` so it is never re-applied; already-applied files are skipped, making the runner idempotent. A missing or empty migrations directory is a no-op (exit 0), since `0001_init.sql` and the migrations directory itself are later steps. On success it prints each newly applied filename and exits cleanly. A same-change test (`test/migrate.test.ts`) exercises the runner against a uniquely-named temp migration directory without touching `src/server/migrations/`.

CONSTRAINTS
- `migrate.ts` exposes an exported `runMigrations(migrationsDir?: string)` defaulting to `import.meta.dir + '/migrations'`, with a direct-execution guard (`if (import.meta.main)`) so `bun run src/server/migrate.ts` auto-runs it with the default; the test imports and calls `runMigrations(tempDir)` against a uniquely named temp dir and the real `src/server/migrations/` is never touched. [from: Q1]
- This is a new file (`src/server/migrate.ts`); it does not exist yet. Do NOT create, import, or reference `src/server/seed.ts`, `src/server/index.ts`, `src/shared/schema.ts`, or `src/server/migrations/` as existing modules or stubs — they are later steps. [from: spec]
- The `migrate` script in `package.json` already exists and must be left byte-for-byte as-is: `"migrate": "bun run src/server/migrate.ts"`. Do not add, rename, or remove any script, dependency, or devDependency. [from: spec]

GOAL
Create `src/server/seed.ts` — the admin-seeding script that backs the existing `"seed": "bun run src/server/seed.ts"` package.json script (the file does not exist yet). The guard is a plain check-then-insert, no transaction. Re-running when an admin already exists is a no-op: it inserts no second admin and leaves the existing row's `phone` / `display_name` / `password_hash` unchanged. - The admin-exists guard is a plain check-then-insert: `SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE role = 'admin'` via `queryFirst`; skip with a log if an admin row is found, else INSERT. No `withTransaction` (single-process seed CLI). [from: Q2]

spec:
GOAL

Create `src/shared/schema.ts` — the single source of truth for shared Zod schemas and their `z.infer`-derived TypeScript types across the listing, auth, and invite domain slices. It defines the five closed-set enums (`generation`, `part_type`, `condition`, `status`, `role`), a single shared E.164 phone schema that strips spaces (U+0020, U+00A0) and dashes (`-`) and then validates the stripped value against `/^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$/`, yielding a normalized E.164 string, and named `export const <name>Schema` Zod exports plus `z.infer`/`z.input` type exports for: phone (raw + normalized), login body, invite create/validate/redeem, and listing create/update/row. The file is pure Zod + inferred types only — no routes, no DB access, no env reads — and ships with a pure-Zod `bun:test` suite in `test/shared-schema.test.ts` that exercises phone normalization (strip + invalid rejections) and every field bound, so downstream steps 12/15/16/18/20/22/23/24/25 can `import { …Schema, …Type } from '../shared/schema.ts'` against stable names.

CONSTRAINTS

- File location is exactly `src/shared/schema.ts`; do not create a barrel `src/shared/index.ts`, do not split into `schema/auth.ts` + `schema/listing.ts` + `schema/invite.ts`, and do not create any file outside `src/shared/`. [from: spec]
- The only new files this task may create are `src/shared/schema.ts` and `test/shared-schema.test.ts`. [from: spec]
- Do not touch `src/server/`, `src/client/`, `ct/`, `build.ts`, `package.json` (scripts or dependencies), `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `.prettierrc.cjs`, `docker-compose.dev.yml`, `.env`, or any migration; `zod` 4.4.3 is already pinned — add zero new `package.json` entries. [from: spec]
- Do NOT define any HTTP route, Hono handler, middleware, `hc<AppType>` client, React component, or test fixture in `schema.ts`; export Zod schemas and `z.infer`/`z.input` types only. No side effects, no `import from './db.ts'`, no `Bun.env`/`process.env` reads. [from: spec]
- Do NOT invent a `me`-response or session-cookie type, and do NOT add `token_hash`, `sessionCookieName`, or `SESSION_DAYS` constants — those belong to step 15 `src/server/auth.ts`. [from: spec]
- Zod 4.4.3 API: import as `import {z} from 'zod'` (bare specifier, NOT `zod/v4`); use `z.enum([...])` for the closed sets; use `z.string().min()/max()/regex()` and `z.number().int()` per the pinned Zod 4 API — confirm names against the installed 4.4.3, do not guess from memory. [from: spec]
- Every exported Zod schema must be an `export const <name>Schema`; every exported type must be `export type X = z.infer<typeof xSchema>` (use `z.input` where a schema's raw-input type is the intended shape). No `any`, no manual `interface` duplicating a schema shape. [from: spec]
- Enum values carried verbatim from the pinned contracts: `generation` ∈ `'na'|'nb'|'nc'|'nd'`; `part_type` ∈ `'oem'|'aftermarket'`; `condition` ∈ `'new'|'used'`; `status` ∈ `'active'|'sold'`; `role` ∈ `'member'|'admin'`. [from: spec]
- Phone normalization: strip every space (U+0020, U+00A0) and every dash (`-`) before validating; after stripping the value must match `/^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$/`; `.parse()` on a valid input returns the post-strip E.164 string; invalid inputs (no `+`, leading zero after `+`, too few digits, too many digits, residual letters) reject with a `ZodError`. Normalization lives inside the shared schema so login (step 16) and invite redeem (step 20) can parse and use the normalized value directly. [from: spec]
- In Zod 4, `.regex()`/`.min()`/`.max()` on a string schema run against the schema's *input* (pre-transform) value; the E.164 validation must therefore run on the *post-strip* value — either by checking the stripped string inside a `.transform()` callback (a thrown error there becomes a `ZodError` in Zod 4) or via `.pipe()` after the transform. Never place a raw `.regex(/^\+…/)` before the strip, because it would validate the un-stripped input. [from: spec]
- The phone schema is a single shared `const phoneSchema` (strip → validate → transform in one schema), not two separate schemas; its `z.infer` (output) and `z.input` (raw) types are both plain `string`, so the exported `Phone` (normalized) and the raw-phone type are `string` aliases. [from: spec]
- Field bounds live in this file: `title` `.min(1).max(200)`; `description` `.min(1).max(5000)`; `price_cents` `z.number().int().min(0).max(100_000_000)`; `location` optional `.max(200)`; `part_number` optional `.max(100)`; `contact_note` optional `.max(500)` (no server-side default); `display_name` `.min(1).max(80)`; `password` `.min(8).max(200)`; invite `token` `.min(16).max(128)`. - The listing row shape maps 1:1 onto the `listings` columns in `0001_init.sql` (`id`, `seller_id`, `title`, `description`, `price_cents`, `generation`, `part_type`, `condition`, `location`, `part_number`, `contact_note`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`); `location`/`part_number`/`contact_note` are `string | null`. spec:
GOAL

Create `src/server/index.ts` for the mx5-private project: the single Hono app that the rest of the plan's routes will chain onto, plus its same-change `bun test` file. Done looks like: importing `src/server/index.ts` yields a `createApp({ staticRoot })` factory; calling it returns a Hono `app` with `AppType = typeof app` exported (for the future `hc<AppType>` typed client via the `grouping-routes-rpc` pattern). Running `bun run src/server/index.ts` (or the existing `dev` script) starts a `Bun.serve` listener on `PORT` (from env, default 3000) that (a) mounts the `/api` route tree on the app, (b) serves the built client statically from `dist/` (`app.css` + the built JS bundle chunks), (c) falls back any non-`/api` GET to the built `index.html` (SPA fallback; 404 when the file is absent — it is absent at this step, never fake it), and (d) exercises body validation through `@hono/zod-validator`'s `zValidator('json', ...)` wired to the shared zod schemas in `src/shared/schema.ts` on a throwaway `POST /api/_ping` route that validates the body with `inviteCreateBodySchema`. The same-change test (`test/server-index.test.ts`) drives the app in-process via `app.request()` (no live DB, no port binding) against a temp fixture static root and asserts static serving, SPA fallback, 404s, and that `_ping` rejects an invalid body with a 4xx.

CONSTRAINTS

- Create `src/server/index.ts` fresh and do NOT modify any already-built file: `src/server/db.ts`, `src/server/migrate.ts`, `src/server/seed.ts`, `src/shared/schema.ts`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `.prettierrc.cjs`, `.env`, `docker-compose.dev.yml`, `build.ts`, or any migration/seed/test file. [from: spec]
- Preserve existing `package.json` scripts verbatim — the app must be runnable today via the existing `dev` script (`bun run --watch src/server/index.ts`) and via bare `bun run src/server/index.ts`; do not add new npm dependencies beyond what is already pinned (`hono@4.12.27`, `@hono/zod-validator@0.8.0`, `zod@4.4.3`). [from: spec]
- Include a throwaway `POST /api/_ping` demo route that validates its body via `zValidator('json', inviteCreateBodySchema)` imported from `src/shared/schema.ts`; do not include any real route (e.g. `/api/auth/login`) because those belong to later steps, and do not wire `zValidator` only as an unused import — a same-change test must exercise rejection of an invalid body. [from: Q1]
- Resolve the static root as `join(import.meta.dir, '..', '..', 'dist')` (repo-root `dist/`, matching the `import.meta.dir` convention in `src/server/migrate.ts`) with no env override; expose it as an injectable parameter on the app factory (e.g. `createApp({ staticRoot })` defaulting to that path, mirroring `runMigrations(migrationsDir)`) so the same-change test can point it at a temp fixture dir without touching `dist/`; the runtime default remains exactly the repo-root `dist/`. [from: Q2]
- `Bun.serve` is invoked directly in `src/server/index.ts` guarded by `if (import.meta.main)` (mirroring `src/server/migrate.ts` and `src/server/seed.ts`), and `AppType` is exported from `index.ts` as `typeof app`, keeping `index.ts` the canonical single home of both; no separate `serve.ts`, no `routes.ts`/`app.ts` indirection — later steps chain route modules from `src/server/routes/*.ts` directly onto this same `app`. [from: Q3]
- Body validation must go through `@hono/zod-validator`'s `zValidator` wired to schemas imported from `src/shared/schema.ts`; do NOT hand-roll body parsing or duplicate schema shapes inside `index.ts`. [from: spec]
- Use `src/server/db.ts`'s exported `sql` / `queryAll` / `queryFirst` / `queryOne` / `withTransaction` for any DB access introduced here; no string-interpolated SQL; the skeleton must stay DB-free at import time (importing `index.ts` in tests must not trigger queries, since `db.ts` binds `DATABASE_URL` at module load). [from: spec]
- SPA fallback: non-`/api` GET requests must serve the built `dist/index.html` (design §5: "non-`/api` GETs serve the built `index.html`"); static serving must cover `dist/` (client JS chunks + `dist/app.css`); `dist/` and `dist/index.html` are produced by later steps (33/34) and may be absent — the fallback and static routes 404 when artifacts are missing; do not create `index.html` or any client bundle in `dist/`, and do not fake them. [from: spec]
- Honor the existing env: `PORT` (listen) and `APP_URL` (external base URL) from `.env`; do not hardcode `3000` or `http://localhost:3000`. [from: spec]
- Do NOT implement routes owned by later steps (login, logout, me, invites create/validate/redeem, listings CRUD, contact, photos, admin, rate limiting, auth/session middleware). The skeleton's scope is the app + `/api` mount + `_ping` validator demo + static + SPA fallback + 404 handling. [from: spec]
- A same-change test must land in the same change as this new server module: a minimal `bun test` file under `test/` that boots the app via `app.request()` (no live DB) and asserts SPA-fallback / static / 404 behavior plus invalid-body rejection on `_ping`; do NOT build the full test harness (step 13) and do NOT touch `playwright-ct.config.ts` or CT specs (step 14). [from: spec]
- Formatting/lint per existing config: printWidth 120, no semicolons, single quotes, no bracket spacing, `arrowParens: avoid`, LF, 4-space indent, `no-explicit-any: error`, `no-shadow: error`. `bun run lint` (prettier --write, eslint --fix, `tsc --noEmit`) must pass on the new file and the new test file (the tsconfig include covers both `src` and `test`). [from: spec]

GOAL
Build the shared `bun test` API-test infrastructure for the Hono app: `test/api.setup.ts`, `test/helpers.ts`, `test/fixtures.ts`, and a self-test `test/infra.test.ts` that lands in the same change and passes. The setup points the shared `sql` client at a dedicated `mx5_test` database on the same Postgres 18 instance (creating that database if absent via a separate superuser connection outside a transaction), runs `runMigrations()` once before tests, and truncates all five data tables (never `schema_migrations`) between test files. `helpers.ts` exports a small request harness (`appRequest` wrapping `app.request()`, JSON helpers, session-cookie helpers) built on `app`/`createApp`/`AppType` from `src/server/index.ts` plus the `queryAll`/`queryFirst`/`queryOne`/`sql`/`withTransaction` helpers from `src/server/db.ts`. `fixtures.ts` exports `seedUser` (argon2id-hashed password via `Bun.password.hash(pw, 'argon2id')`), `seedSession` (`sha256(value)` in `token_hash`, returning a `name=value` `cookie`), `seedListing` (integer `price_cents`, closed-set `generation`/`part_type`/`condition`/`status`), and `seedPhoto` (`position` 0–4, `byte_size`, fake bytea) — all matching the pinned `0001_init.sql` column shapes verbatim and reusing the zod enums from `src/shared/schema.ts`. `test/infra.test.ts` seeds a user + listing via the fixtures, round-trips them through `queryFirst`, and drives the live `POST /api/_ping` route through `appRequest`, so that `AGENT=1 bun test` exits 0. This harness is the only entry point later route steps (16–32, 49–50) will import; no later route, endpoint, or client code is implemented here.

CONSTRAINTS
- Scope the `DATABASE_URL → mx5_test` override per-file: set it at the module top-level of each test file that needs it (before dynamically importing `src/server/db.ts`), following the existing pattern in `test/migrate.test.ts`; do NOT redirect the entire `bun test` run so `test/db.test.ts` keeps its documented dev-`mx5` behavior. [from: Q1]
- Implement create-if-absent in the harness: open a separate superuser connection (e.g. to `postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/postgres`), check `pg_database` for `mx5_test`, and run `CREATE DATABASE mx5_test` outside a transaction when absent — the harness owns the test database's existence. [from: Q2]
- `DATABASE_URL` for this step's tests MUST point at the separate `mx5_test` database on the same docker-compose Postgres (dev DB is `mx5` per `.env`); the harness MUST run `runMigrations()` before tests and truncate tables between test files. [from: spec]
- Do NOT modify or re-scaffold existing files: `src/server/index.ts`, `src/server/db.ts`, `src/server/migrate.ts`, `src/server/seed.ts`, `src/shared/schema.ts`, `src/server/migrations/0001_init.sql`, `docker-compose.dev.yml`, `.env`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.js`, `ct/`, `playwright-ct.config.ts`, or any `ct/*.spec.tsx`. [from: spec]
- Do NOT implement any later-step route, endpoint, page, or component (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/invites/*`, `/api/listings/*`, `/api/admin/*`, any client code); this step only provides the fixtures and request harness those tests will use, documenting that guarantee in comments — it does not assert endpoints that do not exist yet. [from: spec]
- Preserve the pinned data-model facts verbatim in fixtures and assertions: `users(phone, password_hash, display_name, role, is_banned)` with unique E.164 phone; `sessions(token_hash, user_id, expires_at)`; `listings` columns exactly as in `0001_init.sql` (integer `price_cents`; `generation` 'na'|'nb'|'nc'|'nd'; `part_type` 'oem'|'aftermarket'; `condition` 'new'|'used'; `status` 'active'|'sold' default); `listing_photos(listing_id, position smallint 0–4, full_data, thumb_data, byte_size)` with `unique (listing_id, position)`; all `uuid pk` default `gen_random_uuid()`. [from: spec]
- Every new file must pass the existing toolchain as-is: Prettier style (`printWidth 120`, no semicolons, single quotes, no bracket spacing, `arrowParens: avoid`, LF, 4-space indent) and the type-checked ESLint flat config (`no-explicit-any: error`, `no-shadow: error`, unused-vars `^_` ignore) under strict `tsconfig.json` (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `noUnusedLocals/Parameters`). `bun test`, `bun run lint`, and the existing `test:ct` all exit 0. [from: spec]
- Follow the test-first cadence for this step's own artifacts: `test/infra.test.ts` lands in the same change as the harness and passes before the step is done — the harness files are not "done" without their passing test. [from: spec]
- The per-file truncation MUST exclude `schema_migrations` and MUST cover all five tables (`users`, `invites`, `sessions`, `listings`, `listing_photos`) in one `TRUNCATE ... CASCADE` statement, because re-running `runMigrations()` after truncating `schema_migrations` would re-apply `0001_init.sql` (no `IF NOT EXISTS` on the `CREATE TABLE`s) and truncating only the fixture tables fails on FK constraints.
- `seedPhoto()` MUST supply `byte_size integer not null` (the one NOT NULL column without a default; `content_type` has a default of `'image/webp'`); `position` 0–4 and `unique (listing_id, position)` are enforced by the DB, so fixtures rely on those constraints.
- `seedSession()` MUST store `token_hash = sha256(value)` and define the session cookie NAME as a shared constant in `test/helpers.ts` (auth.ts, step 15, does not define it yet) so later route tests reuse the same name.

GOAL

Finalize the Playwright React component-testing (CT) infrastructure for the mx5-private single-package project (step 14 of 53): bring `playwright-ct.config.ts` to its final in-place form (adding the mandated global `expect.toHaveScreenshot: { animations: 'disabled' }` while preserving everything else), and upgrade the existing dual-mode smoke spec `ct/smoke.spec.tsx` so that, in its Playwright branch, it renders `<Smoke />`, asserts behaviour, and captures a `toHaveScreenshot` baseline. - Do not modify any existing `package.json` entry; `test` (`AGENT=1 bun test && playwright test -c playwright-ct.config.ts`) and `test:ct` (`playwright test -c playwright-ct.config.ts`) already match the design and stay as-is; all pinned dependencies (`@playwright/experimental-ct-react` 1.61.1, `playwright` 1.61.1, `react`/`react-dom` 19.2.7, etc.) must not move [from: spec]
- `ct/smoke.spec.tsx` must stay dual-runnable: the `if (typeof Bun === 'undefined')` Playwright branch vs. `bun:test` else-branch guard must be preserved (or the spec otherwise remain loadable by both runners) so `bun test` discovery and the CT run keep collecting exactly their one disjoint test each [from: spec]

spec:
GOAL
Create `src/server/auth.ts` — the server-side auth core for mx5-private (design §6/§11): argon2id password helpers over `Bun.password.hash(pw, "argon2id")` / `Bun.password.verify(pw, hash)`, session issue (opaque 32-byte random hex token; only `sha256(value)` stored in the pinned `sessions` table; ~30-day expiry; cookie name `session`; `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`; `Secure` only when `NODE_ENV=production`), session verify (sha256 the cookie value, look up `sessions.token_hash`, check expiry, load user), a Hono `sessionMiddleware` (via `createMiddleware` from `hono/factory`) that loads the user onto `c.var.user` (null when absent/invalid/expired/banned — banned sessions are rejected here), and `requireAuth`/`requireAdmin` guard factories (401 unauthenticated; 403 for non-admin) — plus its `bun test` suite in `test/auth.test.ts`, in the same change, using the existing `setupApiTest()` / fixtures / helpers harness against `mx5_test` and exercising the middleware/guards on a locally constructed Hono instance (not the app in `src/server/index.ts`). Done looks like: `bun run lint` (prettier + eslint + `tsc --noEmit`) exits 0, `AGENT=1 bun test` passes with `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/mx5` (dev db for `db.test.ts`; API test files override to `mx5_test` per-file), and `bun run test:ct` still exits 0 (no `ct/` or CT artifacts touched).

CONSTRAINTS
- Import DB primitives `sql` / `queryAll` / `queryFirst` / `queryOne` / `withTransaction` from `src/server/db.ts` and shared schemas/types (`roleSchema`, `phoneSchema`, `Password`, `Role`, etc.) from `src/shared/schema.ts`; do not re-scaffold `db.ts`, `migrate.ts`, `seed.ts`, `index.ts`, the migrations, or the test infra. [from: spec]
- All SQL is parameterized via Bun SQL tagged templates (`import {sql} from 'bun'` is the underlying module — `db.ts` re-exports it); no string interpolation of user values into SQL (design §11). [from: spec]
- Password hashing uses `Bun.password.hash(pw, 'argon2id')` / `Bun.password.verify(pw, hash)` in the exact two-arg shape already used by `src/server/seed.ts` and `test/fixtures.ts`; no new hashing dependency. [from: spec]
- Session tokens are opaque and hashed at rest: store only `sha256(value)` in `sessions.token_hash`, never the raw cookie value. The sha256 must be hex-encoded via `createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex')` with `value = randomBytes(32).toString('hex')` (node:crypto) so fixture-seeded sessions from `test/fixtures.ts` verify byte-identically — the only in-repo proven sha256-hex path is node:crypto; do not substitute `Bun.crypto.subtle`. [from: spec]
- Cookie contract: name `session` (pinned by `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME = 'session'` in `test/fixtures.ts`); flags `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`; `maxAge` ~30 days; `Secure` only when `NODE_ENV=production`; no cookie secret or signed token. [from: spec]
- The `sessions` table shape is pinned by `0001_init.sql` (`id uuid pk`, `token_hash text unique not null`, `user_id uuid references users(id) on delete cascade`, `expires_at timestamptz not null`, `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`); do not alter the migration or add a new one. [from: spec]
- Banned-user gate (design §11, cross-slice contract): a banned user's session is rejected at `sessionMiddleware` (`c.var.user` is null); the listing-filter half is owned by the later listings routes (steps 22–32), not this step. [from: spec]
- Guards enforce role/ownership server-side: `requireAdmin` admits only `role = 'admin'` (values `'member' | 'admin'` per `roleSchema`), 401 when unauthenticated, 403 for authenticated non-admins; `requireAuth` is 401 when no valid session. [from: spec]
- `c.var.user` is null-able and typed so strict TS compiles (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `no-explicit-any: error`, `no-shadow: error`); the user payload never includes `password_hash`; the `Variables`/`Env` typing must stay chainable onto a plain `new Hono()` without forcing Env generics onto `src/server/index.ts`. [from: spec]
- This step creates no HTTP route handlers and chains nothing onto the `app` in `src/server/index.ts`; the login/logout/me handlers are steps 16/17 and must not be implemented or stubbed here; do not touch `src/server/routes/`, the client, or Playwright CT artifacts. [from: spec]
- Tests land in the same change (test-first cadence, design §10): `test/auth.test.ts` uses the existing `bun test` harness — set `process.env.DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/mx5_test'` as a top-level statement before any dynamic imports, `await setupApiTest()`, then dynamically import fixtures/helpers/auth (the `test/migrate.test.ts` / `test/infra.test.ts` pattern). [from: spec]
- The test file exercises the middleware/guards on a locally constructed `new Hono()` instance with the auth middleware/guards chained, using `app.request()` — not the live app from `src/server/index.ts` and not `helpers.ts`'s `appRequest`. [from: spec]
- Style: Prettier `printWidth 120`, no semicolons, single quotes, `arrowParens: avoid`, 4-space indent, LF; `bun run lint` must exit 0. [from: spec]
- `package.json` stays untouched; `Bun.password`, `node:crypto`, `hono` are already available. [from: spec]
- `tsc --noEmit` typechecks both `src` and `test`; `verbatimModuleSyntax` requires `import type` for type-only imports; relative imports use explicit `.ts` extensions (tsconfig `allowImportingTsExtensions: true`). [from: spec]
- Pinned versions when checking docs: Bun 1.3.14, hono 4.12.27 (design §13 says verify against current docs when unsure of `Bun.password` / Hono middleware-variables typing). [from: spec]
- Bun SQL returns `timestamptz` as a JS `Date`, so the expiry check compares the row's `expires_at` against `new Date()`. [from: spec]
- Do not purge expired `sessions` rows on the fly — there is no in-repo precedent and the design does not specify it; the middleware only rejects them. [from: spec]
- `setupApiTest()` already creates `mx5_test` if absent and registers the between-file `TRUNCATE ... CASCADE`; the test file only calls it — no `docker/dev-init` or compose changes. [from: spec]

spec:
GOAL
Implement `POST /api/auth/login` for mx5-private: a new `src/server/routes/auth.ts` Hono sub-app, chained in `src/server/index.ts`'s `createApp` via `app.route('/api/auth', authApp)` ahead of the `/api/*` 404 catch-all, that validates the body with the shared `loginBodySchema` (zod + `@hono/zod-validator`), looks up the user by the schema-normalized E.164 phone, verifies the argon2id hash with the existing `verifyPassword`, and on success issues a session via the existing `issueSession()` from `src/server/auth.ts` (opaque 32-byte value, only `sha256(value)` in `sessions.token_hash`, ~30-day expiry), sets the `session` cookie via the returned `issued.cookie` header value, and returns 200 with the `AuthUser` payload — shipped in the same change with its passing `bun test` API tests in `test/auth.test.ts` per the mandatory test-first cadence.

CONSTRAINTS
- Endpoint is exactly `POST /api/auth/login` with body `{ phone, password }` → on success "sets session cookie, returns user" (§5 API contract); do not rename or reshape it. [from: spec]
- Unknown-phone and wrong-password are indistinguishable: both return 401 with `{ error: 'unauthorized' }` (reusing `requireAuth`'s existing body); 400 is returned only for structurally invalid bodies via the zValidator, since validation runs before the handler. [from: Q1]
- A banned user logging in with valid credentials gets the session issued normally and 200 with the `AuthUser` payload — no 403 gate at login; ban enforcement stays in `sessionMiddleware`/`verifySession`. [from: Q2]
- The route lives in a new `src/server/routes/auth.ts` module (a Hono sub-app: `zValidator('json', loginBodySchema)` → user lookup by normalized phone → `verifyPassword` → `issueSession` → `c.header('Set-Cookie', issued.cookie)` + `c.json(user)`; 401 `{ error: 'unauthorized' }` for unknown-phone-or-wrong-password), chained inside `createApp` in `src/server/index.ts` via `app.route('/api/auth', authApp)` ahead of the `app.all('/api/*')` 404 catch-all. [from: Q3]
- `POST /api/_ping` stays in place — removing it now would break the existing passing `test/infra.test.ts` round-trip tests. [from: Q3]
- The same-change API test lives at `test/auth.test.ts`, mirroring `test/infra.test.ts`'s pattern (per-file `DATABASE_URL` override → `setupApiTest` → dynamic helpers/fixtures imports, seeding with `seedUser`, asserting the 200 `AuthUser` body, `Set-Cookie` presence without `Secure`, no raw cookie value in the body, and a `sessions` row with `token_hash === sha256(cookieValue)`). [from: Q3]
- Build on the existing `src/server/auth.ts` (step 15): import and reuse `issueSession`, `verifyPassword`, `AuthUser`, `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME`; do NOT modify, re-implement, or re-scaffold `src/server/auth.ts`, and do not touch `src/server/db.ts`, `src/server/migrate.ts`, `src/server/seed.ts`, or `src/server/migrations/0001_init.sql`. [from: spec]
- In-place update of the existing `src/server/index.ts` app: preserve every existing behavior — the `POST /api/_ping` route, the static-file/SPA-fallback GET handler (including its 404 JSON for `/api/*` paths), the `/api/*` 404 catch-all, the `createApp` signature, and the exported `app` + `AppType`. The new route must be registered on the `app` instance returned by `createApp` (via `app.route`) so `hc<AppType>` typing flows. [from: spec]
- Do NOT build other routes: `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` (step 17), invites (18–20), rate limiting (21), or anything client-side (step 40+). Write the login handler as a plain chained handler with no rate-limit counter so step 21 can wrap it later. [from: spec]
- The phone is normalized to E.164 by the shared `loginBodySchema` (`phoneSchema`'s transform strips U+0020/U+00A0/dashes and validates `/^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$/`); the DB lookup uses `c.req.valid('json').phone`, i.e. the normalized value. [from: spec]
- Password verification is argon2id via `verifyPassword` (wraps `Bun.password.verify`); the stored hash is never returned or logged. [from: spec]
- Never leak the session cookie's raw value or `token_hash` in the response body; the 200 payload is the `AuthUser` shape (`id`, `phone`, `display_name`, `role`, `is_banned`) — never `password_hash`. [from: spec]
- The `Set-Cookie` header is set from `issued.cookie` exactly as `sessionCookie()` already builds it (`session=<value>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Expires=…`, with `Secure` only when `NODE_ENV=production`); do not re-derive the header. [from: spec]
- Parameterized queries only (Bun SQL tagged templates) — no string interpolation of user values. [from: spec]
- Tests run under `bun test` against the separate `mx5_test` database via the existing harness: `process.env.DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/mx5_test'` BEFORE dynamic imports, then `await setupApiTest()`, then dynamic-import `./helpers.ts` + `./fixtures.ts`, mirroring `test/infra.test.ts`; seed with `seedUser`, assert via `appRequestJSON` and the test `queryFirst`. [from: spec]
- Keep the existing Prettier style (4-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, `arrowParens: avoid`, printWidth 120) and satisfy ESLint (`no-explicit-any: error`, `no-shadow: error`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`); `bun run lint` and `tsc --noEmit` must stay clean. [from: spec]
- Do not change the `sessions` table schema, the cookie name `session`, or the ~30-day TTL. [from: spec]

spec:
GOAL
Implement design §11 "Basic rate-limit on login, invite create, and invite redeem (simple in-memory counter is fine — single Bun process)" in this single Bun-process app. Create a new `src/server/rateLimit.ts` module that exports a Hono middleware factory — `createRateLimit({name, max, windowMs})` built via `createMiddleware` from `hono/factory` — backed by one process-wide in-memory `Map` keyed by `${name}:${clientKey}`, where `clientKey` is the caller's IP: `c.req.clientAddr` when the request is a real Bun fetch event, and a single fixed fallback string when it is not (i.e. `app.request()` test calls, where no live connection exists). When a caller exceeds `max` requests within `windowMs`, the middleware short-circuits with `c.json({error: 'too many requests'}, 429)` before any later middleware or handler runs; otherwise it records the request and calls `await next()`. The module also exports the three per-endpoint threshold constants (login 5/15 min, invite-create 10/1 min, invite-redeem 5/1 min) and a `resetRateLimits()` function that clears the counter map. The three existing routes gain their limiter instance as the FIRST chained handler — before `zValidator`/`sessionMiddleware`/`requireAuth` — so validation, auth, and DB work are skipped when the limit is hit: `POST /api/auth/login` in `src/server/routes/auth.ts`, and `POST /api/invites` plus `POST /api/invites/:token/redeem` in `src/server/routes/invites.ts` — each on its own distinct limit instance/key. The change ships with a new `test/rateLimit.test.ts` (using the `setupApiTest`/`appRequest`/`appRequestJSON`/`seedUser`/`seedSession` harness on `mx5_test`) that, per endpoint, asserts N consecutive passes then 429 on the (N+1)th request and the exact 429 body, calling `resetRateLimits()` between tests; and `test/auth.test.ts` / `test/invites.test.ts` / `test/invites-redeem.test.ts` are updated to call `resetRateLimits()` once at suite start so their cumulative per-process request counts (7 logins, 13 invite-creates, 8 redeems) do not trip the new limiter. All existing behaviour, status codes, and response bodies for non-limited requests are unchanged; the full suite passes under `bun run test`.

CONSTRAINTS
- Thresholds are fixed at login 5 requests / 15 min, invite-create 10 requests / 1 min, invite-redeem 5 requests / 1 min, defined as exported named constants in `src/server/rateLimit.ts`; do NOT raise them to match test traffic — the limiter's job is to be real, and `resetRateLimits()` is the test-side mechanism instead [from: Q1]
- Export a `resetRateLimits()` function from `src/server/rateLimit.ts` that clears the entire counter map; `test/rateLimit.test.ts` calls it (in a `beforeEach` and/or before its N-successes-then-429 block), and the existing `test/auth.test.ts`, `test/invites.test.ts`, and `test/invites-redeem.test.ts` call it once at suite start so their cumulative per-process request counts don't 429 [from: Q1]
- In-memory only: a plain `Map` in the single `src/server/rateLimit.ts` module; no new dependency, no external store, no changes to `package.json`, migrations, `src/shared/schema.ts`, or the data model [from: spec]
- Do not change existing route behaviour, status codes, response bodies, query logic, or the chained handlers' semantics for non-limited requests: login still returns 200 `AuthUser` / 401 `{error: 'unauthorized'}`; invite create still returns 200 `{url}` built from `APP_URL` (with the 401/400 rejection paths); redeem still consumes atomically and returns 200 `AuthUser` / 400 / 404 / 409 bodies exactly as today [from: spec]
- The limiter is prepended as the FIRST handler on each `.post(...)` chain (before `zValidator`/`sessionMiddleware`/`requireAuth`) inside the sub-apps `authApp`/`invitesApp` — not in `src/server/index.ts` — so validation and DB work are skipped when the limit is hit; the existing chained order of the remaining handlers is preserved unchanged [from: spec]
- Each of the three endpoints uses its own limiter instance and its own limit key (the `name` field), so login, invite-create, and invite-redeem counters never share state; a burst of failed logins must not block redeem, etc. [from: spec]
- The client identifier is the request's client address, read as `c.req.clientAddr`, not a session or user id; the design's "simple in-memory counter … single Bun process" implies IP keying, and no per-account keying is introduced [from: spec]
- Because `c.req.clientAddr` is not populated under `app.request()` test calls (no live connection), `src/server/rateLimit.ts` must resolve a client key that is stable per real connection in production and a single fixed fallback string for every `app.request()` call, so all test traffic collapses to one shared key per endpoint — detect the live-connection case without relying on `getConnInfo`/throw-message text (e.g. guard on whether a Bun server/connection is available for the request), and key the counter as `${name}:${clientKey}` [from: spec]
- Do not introduce a persistent store, Redis, or config file; thresholds/window are code constants exported from the module — do not add new env vars to `.env` or to the cross-slice contract [from: spec]
- The limiter counts ALL requests to the endpoint (not only failed ones); a 429 response is emitted before any later middleware/handler runs, so the counter increments for requests that would otherwise 400/401/200 alike [from: spec]
- Preserve the existing test harness contract in the new test file: set `process.env.DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/mx5_test'` and `process.env.APP_URL = 'http://localhost:3000'` at the top BEFORE dynamic imports, call `await setupApiTest()`, and dynamically import `./api.setup.ts` / `./fixtures.ts` / `./helpers.ts` / `../src/server/index.ts` (mirror `test/invites-redeem.test.ts`); use a phone range not already claimed by another test file [from: spec]
- `bun test` runs every test file in ONE process and file order is non-alphabetical readdir order, so the module-level `Map` persists across all test files — every test that exhausts a limit must call `resetRateLimits()` first, and the three existing route test files must call it at suite start, or their cumulative counts will 429 [from: spec]
- Do not touch later-step routes/pages (listings, photos, admin, client) — only the three named endpoints, the new module, and the new/updated test files [from: spec]
- Preserve code style: Prettier (printWidth 120, 4-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, no bracket spacing, arrowParens avoid, one-line `if` without braces for single-statement conditionals) and the existing ESLint typed rules (`no-explicit-any: error`, `no-shadow: error`); no `any`; named types for object literals with >2 properties [from: spec]

GOAL

CONSTRAINTS
- Response envelope is exactly `{items: [...], page, total, pages}` with `total` = total matching rows and `pages = ceil(total/12)`; document this envelope in the `listings.ts` module header comment [from: Q3]
- Sort order is `created_at DESC, id DESC` for `sort=new` (default), and `price_cents ASC/DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC` for `price_asc`/`price_desc`; sort order is SQL syntax, so emit it from a fixed map of the validated 3-value enum to a literal ORDER BY fragment — never interpolate the raw query string [from: Q2]
- Keep zValidator's default 400 response for invalid query params — no hook override (the override would erase the RPC error-union on `hc<AppType>`); in `test/listings.test.ts` assert invalid-param cases by `status === 400` only, never the body shape; reserve the repo's lowercase `{error: '…'}` bodies for handler-emitted errors (401 on `mine=1`) [from: Q1]
- Chain `sessionMiddleware` on the route and, in the handler, when `mine` is present and `c.var.user === null`, return `c.json({error: 'unauthorized'}, 401)`; a banned-but-logged-in caller also gets 401, never an empty list (verifySession resolves banned users to null); `requireAuth` must not be used because it would 401 the anonymous public grid [from: Q4]
- Escape LIKE pattern metacharacters (`%`, `_`, `\`) in `q` so searches are literal substrings (e.g. `?q=100%` matches listings literally containing "100%") [from: Q5]
- `q` searches strictly `(title || ' ' || description)` — the same expression as the existing `idx_listings_search_trgm` GIN index in `0001_init.sql` — and no other columns (no `location`/`part_number`); the ILIKE predicate must be written against that concatenated expression to use the index [from: Q6]
- Do not add any other route to `src/server/routes/listings.ts` in this step — `GET /:id`, `POST /`, `PATCH /:id`, `POST /:id/sold`, `DELETE /:id`, `GET /:id/contact` belong to later steps (23–28) [from: spec]
- Do not modify `src/server/migrations/0001_init.sql` or add a new migration file; the `pg_trgm` extension and `idx_listings_search_trgm` already exist [from: spec]
- Do not touch `src/server/index.ts` beyond the one `app.route('/api/listings', listingsApp)` line and its matching import, placed ahead of the `app.get('/*')` SPA/static handler; do not remove `/api/_ping` or reorder existing mounts/catch-alls [from: spec]
- Do not modify `test/fixtures.ts`, `test/api.setup.ts`, `test/helpers.ts`, or any existing test file's harness; the new list-query schema(s) are the only allowed change to `src/shared/schema.ts`, and they must be composed from the existing `generationSchema`/`partTypeSchema`/`conditionSchema` (no redeclared literal sets) without breaking `test/shared-schema.test.ts` [from: spec]
- Do not introduce a rate limiter on `GET /api/listings` (design §11 mandates rate limits only on login, invite create, invite redeem — already in `src/server/rateLimit.ts`) [from: spec]
- The list payload must not ship `phone`, `seller_id`, or any other seller personal data; the cover photo id (unguessable UUID of the `listing_photos` row at `position = 0`, via LEFT JOIN/subselect selecting only `id` — never the bytea columns) is allowed, or null when the listing has no photos [from: spec]
- All SQL goes through the parameterized tagged-template helpers in `src/server/db.ts` (`queryAll`/`queryFirst`/`sql`); no string interpolation of user values; lowercase-phrase `{error: '…'}` bodies for handler errors [from: spec]

- Do not change `package.json` scripts or dependencies; only import from the already-used set (`hono`, `zod`, `@hono/zod-validator`, `bun`, `../db.ts`, `../auth.ts`, `../../shared/schema.ts`) [from: spec]

- `q` absent or empty-after-trim is treated as "no filter" (the ILIKE clause is skipped); all enum/sort param values are lowercase-only via the shared zod enums [from: spec]

spec:
GOAL
Add the `GET /api/listings/:id` detail route to the existing `listingsApp` Hono instance in `src/server/routes/listings.ts`, registered via `listingsApp.get('/:id', ...)` ahead of nothing else in that module (the app-level SPA fallback and JSON 404 in `src/server/index.ts` already sit after every `/api` route, so no `index.ts` change is needed). For a single visible listing the handler returns the full `listings` row as a 1:1 mirror of `listingRowSchema` (id, seller_id, title, description, price_cents, generation, part_type, condition, status, location, part_number, contact_note, created_at, updated_at), spread flat at the top level, plus a top-level `display_name` (the seller's, joined from `users`) and a top-level `photo_ids` (a `string[]` of the raw UUIDs of every `listing_photos` row for that listing, ordered by `position` ASC — an empty array, not null, when the listing has no photos). The response shape is exactly `{...listingRow, display_name, photo_ids}` — no seller nesting, key is `photo_ids` not `photos`. The route is public (no session middleware, no auth guard); the only seller data selected is `display_name` (plus `seller_id`, which lives in the `listings` row itself), so the seller's `phone` is withheld by construction. Nonexistent, malformed (non-UUID), or banned-seller ids all return 404 with body exactly `{error: 'not found'}` — matching the `src/server/index.ts` catch-all shape verbatim. The `:id` path param is always a bound parameter in the `db.ts` tagged templates, never string-interpolated. The change lands with its own `bun test` coverage in the same change, in a new `test/listings.detail.test.ts` following the identical in-process harness pattern as `test/listings.test.ts`; the route module's header comment is updated to reflect that `GET /:id` is no longer a "later step". Done means the route is registered, its tests exist and pass in the same change, and `bun run test` + `bun run lint` are both green.

CONSTRAINTS
- The response envelope is flat: the full `listingRowSchema` columns spread at the top level, plus a top-level `display_name` (string) and a top-level `photo_ids` (`string[]` of raw UUIDs, `[]` when the listing has no photos); no seller object nesting, and the key is `photo_ids`, not `photos`. [from: Q1]
- The 404 body for this route is exactly `{error: 'not found'}` (status 404), matching the `src/server/index.ts` catch-all shape verbatim; this overrides the module-local named-message pattern used by `invitesApp` (e.g. `{error: 'invite not found'}`). [from: Q2]
- Never ship the seller's `phone` (or any phone-like field) in the detail payload — design §11: "Phone reveal only to authenticated members; never ship phone in list/detail payloads." The only seller data selected is `display_name` (plus `seller_id`, which is a column of `listings` itself, not a `users` join). Do not add a `GET /:id/contact` endpoint (that is step 28). [from: spec]
- Listings whose seller has `is_banned = true` are excluded: a banned-seller listing must 404 exactly like a missing id — the lookup uses `JOIN users u ON u.id = l.seller_id ... AND u.is_banned = false` (the same filter the `GET /` grid uses), and no distinct error code leaks the banned seller's existence. [from: spec]
- The route requires no session/auth at all: no `sessionMiddleware`, no `requireAuth` — anonymous callers can read a full listing (same as `GET /api/listings`); the phone is withheld by construction (it is simply not selected), not by a guard. [from: spec]
- Nonexistent, malformed (non-UUID), or banned-seller `:id` all return 404 with the same body; a malformed value must not reach Postgres as a raw uuid-column comparison that would raise `invalid input syntax for type uuid` → 500. Either shape-check the param before querying (the `invitesApp` `tokenSchema.safeParse(...)` pattern) or catch the coercion error and answer the same 404 — the observable behaviour pinned is: malformed input → 404 `{error: 'not found'}`. [from: spec]
- Keep all user-supplied values (the `:id` path param) as bound parameters in the `db.ts` tagged templates (`queryFirst`/`queryAll`); no string interpolation of `id` into SQL (design §11). [from: spec]
- Do not modify the existing `GET /` handler, its `listingListQuerySchema`, any other route module, or `src/server/index.ts`; do not create new shared schemas beyond what this response needs — reuse `ListingRow`/the shared enums from `src/shared/schema.ts` (a local `type` in the route module is the pattern used for `ListingCardRow`; `AppType` is `typeof app` in `index.ts`, so the new route flows into it automatically — do not hand-roll response types on the server). [from: spec]
- Do not touch step 31's `GET /api/photos/:id`, step 24's `POST /api/listings`, or any client code — this task is the server route and its tests only. [from: spec]
- Tests land in the same change as the route (design §10 test-first cadence: "No route or component is considered done until its test exists and passes."), in a new `test/listings.detail.test.ts` using the in-process harness exactly as `test/listings.test.ts` does: `process.env.DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/mx5_test'` override at the very top before all dynamic imports, `await setupApiTest()` from `./api.setup.ts`, then dynamic imports of `./fixtures.ts`, `./helpers.ts`, and `../src/server/index.ts`; seed fresh fixtures per test (rows persist across `test()` calls within a file). No Playwright component test is needed (server route only). [from: spec]
- Style: Prettier printWidth 120, no semicolons, single quotes, `arrowParens: avoid`, LF (formatting otherwise left to the project's Prettier config — no non-standard indent value); ESLint flat config constraints (`no-explicit-any: error`, `@typescript-eslint/no-shadow: error`, `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`) must hold under `bun run lint`. [from: spec]
- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on: the 200 lookup must use `queryFirst<T>` (returns `T | undefined`), not `queryOne<T>` (which throws on 0 rows — wrong helper for a 404 path). [from: spec]
- Update the `src/server/routes/listings.ts` header comment when adding the detail route (it currently lists `GET /:id` under "land in later steps"). [from: spec]

GOAL
Add the authenticated create-listing route `POST /api/listings` to the existing `listingsApp` in `src/server/routes/listings.ts` (already mounted at `/api/listings` in `src/server/index.ts`), and land its passing API test in the same change. The route chains `sessionMiddleware` → `requireAuth` → `zValidator('json', listingCreateSchema)` and, on success (200 or 201), inserts a single `listings` row whose `seller_id` is taken from the authenticated session (`c.var.user.id`, never the body) plus the caller-provided fields from `c.req.valid('json')` (title, description, price_cents, generation, part_type, condition, status defaulting to `'active'`, optional location/part_number/contact_note), via a parameterized `INSERT ... RETURNING id` (id is the `gen_random_uuid()` column default). It responds with the new listing's `id`. Photos are intentionally NOT part of this route — they land in a later step via `POST /api/listings/:id/photos`. The test covers: creation returns a usable id and the row reads back, 401 for unauthenticated (and banned) callers, 400 for schema-invalid bodies (zValidator's default response), and that `seller_id` is server-assigned — a client-supplied `seller_id`/`id`/timestamp is stripped by zod (not a 400) and the stored `seller_id`/`id` always equal the session user's and the returned id. The test is appended to the existing `test/listings.test.ts` (reusing its module-level seeded owner/other/banned users and `mkListing`-style helpers) and must pass under `AGENT=1 bun test` against `mx5_test`, with `bun run lint` clean and the existing GET routes and their tests preserved.

CONSTRAINTS
- Edit only `src/server/routes/listings.ts` (add the `listingsApp.post('/')` handler) and the listings API test under `test/`; do NOT touch `src/server/index.ts` (the `/api/listings` mount and `AppType` export already exist), `src/shared/schema.ts` (`listingCreateSchema` is authoritative for field names, bounds, and the `status` default), `src/server/auth.ts`, `src/server/db.ts`, migrations, or the existing fixtures/helpers. [from: spec]
- Do NOT implement or stub any other listings route (`PATCH /:id`, `POST /:id/sold`, `DELETE /:id`, `GET /:id/contact`) and do NOT add any photo handling (no multipart, no `listing_photos` inserts) — that is a later step's job. [from: spec]
- Chain the existing `sessionMiddleware` + `requireAuth` from `src/server/auth.ts` so the route returns 401 `{error:'unauthorized'}` for absent/invalid/expired sessions and for banned users (a banned session resolves to a null user), and still keep a defensive `if (c.var.user === null) return c.json({error:'unauthorized'},401)` guard inside the handler, matching the `routes/invites.ts` in-repo pattern. [from: spec]
- Validate the body with `zValidator('json', listingCreateSchema)` using the default 400 response on failure (no hook override), consistent with the existing route style in the file. [from: spec]
- Every inserted value (all caller fields and the session user id) must be a bound parameter in a `db.ts` tagged template — no string interpolation into SQL; never trust the client for `seller_id`, `id`, `created_at`, or `updated_at` (on create the column defaults `gen_random_uuid()`, `now()`, `now()` suffice; this step adds no UPDATE). [from: spec]
- Do NOT add a rate limiter to this route (design §11 limits only login, invite create, and invite redeem). [from: spec]
- Follow the existing harness pattern verbatim in the test: per-file top `process.env.DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://mx5:mx5@localhost:5432/mx5_test'` before the dynamic imports, `setupApiTest()`, then dynamic `import('./fixtures.ts')` / `import('./helpers.ts')` / `import('../src/server/index.ts')`; seed via `seedUser`/`seedSession`; assert via `appRequest`/`appRequestJSON`; rows persist across tests within the file (TRUNCATE is per-file in `afterAll`), so each new test must scope with its own unique token/tag. [from: spec]
- Prettier (printWidth 120, no semicolons, single quotes, 4-space indent, no bracket spacing) and ESLint `recommendedTypeChecked` (`no-explicit-any: error`, `@typescript-eslint/no-shadow: error`) must pass — `bun run lint` clean. [from: spec]
- Preserve every existing behavior of `listingsApp` (GET `/` grid and GET `/:id` detail) and all their tests; this change is additive only. [from: spec]
- Use zod's default strip-and-succeed behavior for unknown keys: a body that also carries `seller_id` (and/or `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) must still succeed (200 or 201), and the test must then read the row back via the `queryFirst` helper and assert `seller_id === <seeded session user's id>` and the row's `id` matches the returned id — do NOT reject unknown keys with a 400. [from: Q1]

GOAL
Add the owner-only `PATCH /api/listings/:id` route (design §5) to the existing `listingsApp` in `src/server/routes/listings.ts`, chained as `sessionMiddleware` → `requireAuth` → malformed-UUID 404 guard → ownership + banned-seller check → `zValidator('json', listingUpdateSchema)` → dynamic partial-UPDATE handler, and land its `bun test` suite in the same change appended to the existing `test/listings.test.ts`. The app mount in `src/server/index.ts` (`app.route('/api/listings', listingsApp)`) is unchanged. The handler runs a partial `UPDATE … RETURNING *` where only the fields present in the validated body are set, an explicit `null` clears `location`/`part_number`/`contact_note`, `updated_at` is set by the application to `now()` on every UPDATE (no trigger — no database-side timestamp handling is added), and the response is 200 with the updated full row: exactly the 14 `listingRowSchema` fields (`id`, `seller_id`, `title`, `description`, `price_cents`, `generation`, `part_type`, `condition`, `status`, `location`, `part_number`, `contact_note`, `created_at`, `updated_at`), matching the `GET /:id` row shape minus `display_name`/`photo_ids`. Nonexistent, malformed (non-UUID), non-owner, and banned-seller ids all return 404 `{error: 'not found'}`; unauthenticated and banned callers get 401 `{error: 'unauthorized'}`; schema-invalid bodies get 400 via the validator's default. The route is done only when its tests exist and pass under `AGENT=1 bun test` against the `mx5_test` database, alongside the existing `GET /api/listings`, `GET /api/listings/:id`, and `POST /api/listings` suites.

CONSTRAINTS
